title: Primer
tagline: GitHub's design system: React components and CSS with accessibility in the API.
note: The reference for doing enterprise UI without enterprise slop. Steal Primer React's composition model and its focus-management discipline — accessibility lives in the component contract, not in a docs footnote.

title: Polaris
tagline: Shopify's system for admin interfaces, strong on judgment over widgets.
note: The rare system that teaches when not to use a pattern. Read the content and information-architecture guidance before touching the components — that's where the value is.

title: Atlassian Design System
tagline: Foundations with unusual depth on content, terminology, and tokens.
note: Go for the foundations, stay for the terminology pages. Few public systems take naming and content standards this seriously — steal the habit of documenting words alongside components.

title: Carbon
tagline: IBM's data-dense enterprise system, open-sourced with unusual rigor.
note: The data-table and dashboard guidance is the best public reference for dense UI. Steal the spacing rhythm that keeps 12-column data grids readable instead of merely present.

title: Material Design 3
tagline: Google's full-stack spec: color, type, motion, and interaction in one place.
note: Overkill as a whole, invaluable in parts. Steal the motion tokens and easing guidance — it's the most complete public motion spec — and ignore the parts that would make your product look like Google.

title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
tagline: The platform canon on restraint: every control justified by a human reason.
note: Still the best writing on saying no. Read any single control's page to see how Apple reasons from human capability to pixel — then apply that reasoning to your own components.

title: Fluent 2
tagline: Microsoft's cross-platform tokens with per-component accessibility requirements.
note: Worth studying for the token architecture across platforms and the way accessibility requirements are stated per component rather than in a separate chapter nobody reads.

title: Spectrum
tagline: Adobe's system, notable for cleanly layered global, alias, and component tokens.
note: Spectrum Tokens is the clearest public example of token layering done right: base scales stay dumb, aliases carry intent, components never touch raw values. Copy the layering, whatever your scale.

title: Lightning Design System
tagline: Salesforce's blueprints for dense admin UI, with a pragmatic utility escape hatch.
note: If your product has settings pages, record views, or data entry, start here. Steal the blueprint concept — full-page patterns, not just components — and the honesty about when to break out to utilities.

title: Base Web
tagline: Uber's React system built on overrides instead of theming props.
note: A genuinely different answer to customization: deep overrides rather than a theme object. Worth studying before you decide your own system's extension model — it makes different trade-offs than everything else on this list.

title: GOV.UK Design System
tagline: Proof that boring is a feature: tested patterns starting from user needs.
note: Every pattern ships with research behind it. When a stakeholder asks for a clever form interaction, this is the citation that ends the discussion — and the form patterns themselves are flawless.

title: U.S. Web Design System
tagline: The federal system, with maturity and contribution guidance worth copying.
note: Beyond the components, steal the maturity model: it gives teams an honest ladder from ad-hoc pages to a real system. The contribution docs are a template for any public-sector or open-source system.

title: Pajamas
tagline: GitLab's Figma-first system with honest docs about what's stable.
note: Refreshingly transparent about component maturity and design-to-code gaps. Worth reading for any team where Figma leads and code follows — the handoff documentation is the product.

title: Stacks
tagline: Stack Overflow's utility-first CSS with atomic classes and content guidelines.
note: Atomic CSS before it was fashionable, plus content guidelines most developer tools skip. Steal the restraint: a small set of utilities composed well beats a sprawling component API.

title: BBC GEL
tagline: The BBC's global experience language, with accessibility as the first chapter.
note: Designed for everyone on every device, in any language, on any bandwidth. The accessibility and inclusive-design foundations are the ones to assign to anyone who thinks systems are about buttons.
